newsitem.title: USA: Coca-Cola Enterprises pours bonds into thirsty mkt.
newsitem.headline: Coca-Cola Enterprises pours bonds into thirsty mkt.

text.p: Coca-Cola Enterprises Inc's debt offering is expected to quench investor thirst for corporate paper on Tuesday, amid a temporary drought of supply, syndicate sources said.
The A3/A-plus rated deal, which was initially rumored to come at a size of between $600-$750 million, has been launched at a size of $600 million, but may grow larger, syndicate sources said.
"It's the only game in town right now ... the deal will probably grow in size," said one high-grade syndicate source.
Although a calendar was building for later in the week, players said, supply had been temporarily shelved ahead of Federal Reserve Alan Greenspan's Humphrey Hawkins testimony on Tuesday.
The first tranche was to consist of $200 million in four-year debt and was expected to price at a spread of between 30-32 basis points over Treasuriees.
The second tranche was to consist of $200 million in seven-year debt and was expected to price at 40-42 basis points over Treasuries.
The final tranche was to include a 20-year issue which was seen pricing at a spread of 60 basis points over Treasuries, sources ssaid.
All maturities were expected to be noncallable for life, they said.
Lehman Brothers was expected to serve as lead underwriter for the offering, sources said.
